content.text: Ten seconds, realistic historical film, one continuous first-person eye-level view, the exact same wounded grey-robed man and linen army tent as image 1. Preserve his face, dark cloth head wrap, posture on the straw bed, lighting, rough paper and army clothes. Continue the action of retrieving ONE folded paper from his pouch. The camera is the recipient. He hands this same paper forward to the viewer. Two ordinary hands belonging to the viewer enter from below and take its two lower corners. Show real contact and weight transfer. The man lets go ONLY after the viewer securely holds it, and retracts both his hands. From then until the end, the viewer keeps this same paper. No repeated transfer. Crucially, the ONLY surface of this paper ever seen by the camera is its plain, COMPLETELY BLANK REVERSE. The side with any marks ALWAYS faces away from the camera toward the man. Never rotate the front toward the lens. No writing, lines, ink, stamps, letters, symbols, diagrams, titles, subtitles, labels, cards or UI appear anywhere. Keep the paper at a natural oblique angle, a little below the man's face; no giant page covering the frame. Fibers and creases are visible, normal fingers, coherent hands, no hands passing through paper. Timing: 0-2 seconds finish drawing the paper; 2-5 seconds offer and recipient takes the paper; 5-6 seconds man releases and withdraws; 6-10 seconds quiet eye contact while recipient steadily holds the blank reverse in the foreground. He does not point yet. His mouth stays closed throughout: no speech, no narration, no vocal sound. Only synchronized cloth and paper rustles, tent wind. No music, no BGM, no score. No masks, blur patches, mosaic, local defocus, black boxes, color rectangles or editorial overlays.
